 Cody Johnson to skip 2026 CMA Awards, cites mental and physical exhaustion 
 1:59 Headlines from ABC News Live Isabelle Clayton/Redferns By Shafiq Najib November 18, 2026, 3:33 PM 
 Country music star Cody Johnson says he will not attend the 2026 CMA Awards as he takes time off to focus on his health.
 Johnson, 39, who was scheduled to perform at Wednesday's awards show, announced Tuesday on Instagram that he was experiencing "mental and physical exhaustion."
 "After getting sick at the end of my UK tour earlier this month, I realized much of it stemmed from mental and physical exhaustion," Johnson wrote. "I want to be open about this because I believe we help one another by revealing our truths, and this time my truth isn't in the words of a song; it's real life."
 Related 2026 CMA Awards: How to watch, who is performing and more The singer said he plans to spend time at home with his family as he recovers.
 "At the end of the day, I'm a human being, no matter how much I tell myself and others I'm Superman," he wrote. "I have everything to be thankful for, but sometimes I put too much pressure on myself."
 Johnson continued, "I'm going to spend some time recouping at home; being grounded by my family is what I need most right now."
 Cody Johnson performs on October 24, 2026 in Manchester, England. Isabelle Clayton/Redferns The announcement comes after Johnson canceled concerts in Belfast and Dublin earlier this month after being diagnosed with a viral infection.

 In his statement Tuesday, Johnson also reflected on the demands of his career and thanked fans for their support.
 "I've waited my whole life to be where I am in my career, and I wouldn't have it any other way," he wrote. "It was well worth the wait and the hard work it took to get here. However, going 100 mph all the time isn't healthy, and I see that now."
 Johnson said he plans to take time off through the end of the year, concluding his statement, "I will see you all in 2027."
 Related CMA Awards 2026: Taylor Swift, Ella Langley lead list of nominees Johnson is nominated for four CMA Awards this year, including entertainer of the year, male vocalist of the year, single of the year and music video of the year. His song "The Fall" is nominated in the latter two categories.
 The 60th annual CMA Awards, hosted by Lainey Wilson, will air live Wednesday, Nov. 18, at 8 p.m. ET on ABC and Disney+, with next-day streaming available on Hulu.
